title: Detention and Yearbook
premise: Dominic Montrose, seventeen and de facto parent to his two younger siblings, discovers that a group chat of classmates is receiving messages describing events days before they occur — small at first, then a prediction that names his sister. As the school investigates and friendships fracture over what to do with foreknowledge, Dominic realizes the messages trace back to his late father's unfinished yearbook project, a machine-adjacent experiment he inherited without knowing it. To protect his family, he must expose the truth, sacrificing the careful anonymity he's built, and in the final chapter he chooses honesty over control, graduating with the labels stripped away and the future finally unwritten.
about_author: Isandro Sterling is the pen name of a former night-shift paramedic who writes young adult fiction about kids who grow up too fast. He lives near the coast with an ancient dog and a suspiciously organized bookshelf.

chapters.title: The Careful Boy
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A morning routine montage: packing lunches, signing permission slips, hiding exhaustion behind straight-A composure. Establishes siblings Marisol (12) and Theo (8) and mom's night shifts. Emotional beat: love expressed as vigilance, and the quiet ache of being nobody's kid anymore.

chapters.title: Group Chat: Unknown Number
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. An anonymous message appears in a class group chat predicting a fire drill three days early. It happens exactly as described. Most students laugh it off; Dominic, who plans everything, feels something cold turn over. Beat: curiosity cracking the shell of routine.

chapters.title: The Yearbook Committee
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The school yearbook committee — Priya, Jules, Marcus, quiet Wren — admits they've been getting predictions for weeks and haven't told anyone. They recruit Dominic for his discretion. Beat: reluctant belonging; being needed for the first time as himself, not as caretaker.

chapters.title: Small Prophecies
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Predictions escalate from trivial to personal: a pop quiz, a breakup, then a car accident on Route 9 that Dominic can't prevent despite warning them obliquely. Guilt lands hard. Beat: the first taste of responsibility for knowledge he never asked for.

chapters.title: Marisol's Name
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A new message arrives: 'MONTROSE. THURSDAY. STAIRWELL.' Dominic spirals into protective overdrive, shadowing his sister at school until she snaps at him for smothering her. Beat: care curdling into control; the cost of loving through fear.

chapters.title: Thursday
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Thursday comes and goes with nothing — until Marisol catches a falling student on the stairwell, breaking her wrist. The prediction was real but misread. Beat: relief and horror entwined; foreknowledge is a riddle, not a shield.

chapters.title: Jules Wants to Win
chapters.summary: Jules's POV. Jules starts using predictions for advantage — betting, blackmail-lite, social climbing — and pressures the group to stay silent. Dominic objects; the committee splits. Beat: loyalty tested against conscience within the friend group.

chapters.title: Dad's Boxes
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Hunting for answers, Dominic opens his father's stored boxes and finds the senior yearbook his dad never finished — plus notebooks full of probability models, pattern-tracking, and a prototype 'forecast' system built with a teacher, Mr. Okafor. Beat: inheritance revealed; grief given a shape.

chapters.title: Mr. Okafor's Office
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The retired teacher admits he and Dominic's father built a predictive engine as a student project decades ago, dormant until someone reactivated it this semester. He doesn't know who. Beat: the past reaching forward; adults admitting their own unfinished stories.

chapters.title: Wren Knows Something
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, the committee's ghost, has been feeding the chat — not with predictions, but by reactivating her grandfather Okafor's old server as a memorial to her own dead parent. She didn't expect it to work. Beat: guilt and loneliness mirrored between Wren and Dominic.

chapters.title: Shutdown Fails
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The group tries to kill the server, but the model has been scraping school data autonomously and now generates its own forecasts. One new prediction appears unsent, addressed to Dominic alone. Beat: loss of control; the machine has outgrown its makers.

chapters.title: The Private Message
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The private forecast reads: 'MONTCROSE HOUSE. FIRE. 11 DAYS.' Dominic faces an impossible choice — evacuate quietly and look insane, or tell the truth about everything. Beat: the central dilemma crystallized; protection versus honesty.

chapters.title: Mom Comes Home Early
chapters.summary: Mom's POV. Mom senses the strain, takes a rare morning off, and finds the notebooks. Instead of anger, she tells him about the years she spent letting him carry too much, and how his father died chasing certainty. Beat: the weight begins to be shared; permission to be seventeen.

chapters.title: Telling the Committee
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Dominic confesses everything to the group — the house, the machine, his family. Jules wants to leak selectively for leverage; Priya proposes going public before graduation. Vote splits 2–2 with Wren abstaining. Beat: fracture point; every loyalty now costs something.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Jules's POV. Jules leaks partial predictions to the school paper, framing the committee as heroes and omitting the danger. Suspicion falls on Dominic's 'unstable' household. Beat: betrayal by a friend who was also scared; reputation as a weapon.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The principal and a district investigator question Dominic, implying his home life explains 'the hoax.' He almost lies to protect himself — and instead tells the whole truth, including his father's role. Beat: the careful boy chooses exposure over safety.

chapters.title: Day Nine
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, sensing tension, packs a go-bag of stuffed animals and snacks 'just in case,' revealing he's understood more than anyone knew. Dominic realizes his siblings have been protecting him back. Beat: tenderness under terror; family as mutual shelter.

chapters.title: Confronting the Machine
chapters.summary: Dominic and Wren's POV. At the server, they find the fire forecast is a false positive born of corrupted data — but the machine also outputs one true, verifiable warning buried in noise. They must decide which predictions deserve belief. Beat: climax approach; judgment replacing prophecy.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The predicted hour arrives. Thanks to honest warnings, the school evacuates the wing where an electrical fault genuinely ignites — no one hurt. The false house-fire forecast dissolves. Beat: climax resolved not by magic but by people choosing to act on shared truth.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The story breaks publicly; the machine is dismantled, Okafor honored, Jules faces consequences but apologizes without excuses. Dominic is interviewed and refuses to be cast as either victim or hero. Beat: labels offered and declined; identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Yearbook Signatures
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The committee finishes the abandoned yearbook, adding his father's name to the credits. Marisol's cast comes off; Theo signs the first page. Dominic writes honest, unguarded messages in friends' books for the first time. Beat: memory made deliberate; inheritance accepted on his terms.

chapters.title: Graduation, Unwritten
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At graduation, no predictions arrive — the future is blank again. Walking across the stage, Dominic lets himself want things: college nearby, mornings that belong to him. Final beat: he stops being careful and starts being free.
